title: Births and deaths
description: Every particle gives birth at rate λ = 0.6 (the child starts at its parent's position) and dies at rate μ = 0.4, with independent exponential clocks. The number of particles $N(t)$ is a linear birth–death process with $\mathbb{E}N(t) = N_0 e^{(\lambda-\mu)t}$. The Birth / death window shows your run, this expectation and the 5–95 % band of 200 independent runs. The density follows a Fokker–Planck equation with a reaction term, $\partial_t\rho = \nabla\cdot(\rho\nabla\Psi) + \frac{\sigma^2}{2}\Delta\rho + (\lambda - \mu)\rho$.

questions.text: Expected number of particles at $t = 5$, starting from $N_0 = 100$?
Does your run stay inside the band? How wide is the band at $t = 5$ compared with its mean?
Set λ = μ = 0.5 and restart the plot. For λ = μ, $\mathrm{Var}\,N(t) = 2N_0\lambda t$. Standard deviation at $t = 4$ for $N_0 = 100$?
With λ = μ the expected number is constant. What happens to a single run in the long run, and why?
